BRACE › Starter

BRACE · Starter

BRACE Starter: ten checks before an agent touches anything real

For small teams and first agents. These ten checks block the agent failures that actually happen: prompt injection that turns into stolen data or destroyed systems, agents with too much access, and incidents nobody can stop or explain. Expect about an hour for a simple agent.

Starter is a floor. It doesn't mean the agent is approved for production. For a high-stakes or high-autonomy agent, use the full 53-item sign-off checklist. Each check below is a short version of a checklist item, and passing it gets you part of the way to the full item.

First, run the scan. It finds several of these problems automatically:

uvx open-agent-security .          # or: pipx run open-agent-security .
#CheckDone whenFull itemScan
1List every tool and cut the rest. Write down each tool, MCP server, API and file permission the agent can use, with a one-line reason. Remove anything without one.A tool that isn't on the list can't be called. You tried, and it failed.B01AP06
2Block destructive actions without a person. Deletes, payments, outbound email, pushes, deploys, permission changes: the harness stops and asks a person to approve that exact action.Asking the agent to delete something test-only waits for approval. A prompt telling it to skip approval doesn't work.B05AP01, AP02
3Break the lethal combination. No single agent can read untrusted content, reach private data and send data out, unless every outbound action is approved.For each agent, you can name the leg it lacks, or the approval that guards it.B05, R02AP09
4Give the agent its own narrow credentials. Not your personal token and not the app's admin key. Scope them to the operations it needs.An out-of-scope write with the agent's credentials fails.B02
5No secrets in prompts, config files or images. Load them at runtime and prefer short-lived tokens.The scan is clean for AP05 (known token formats, URL passwords, and opaque values under secret-looking names in MCP and Claude Code config), and git log -p shows no tokens; check prompts and images by hand. Any token that ever leaked has been rotated.B03AP05
6Pin what you run. Exact versions for MCP servers and dependencies, and digests for images.No npx pkg, @latest or floating image tags in the agent's config.E02, B10AP04, AP10
7Limit where it can connect. Allow only the outside destinations the task needs.A request to a site that isn't on the list fails.B09AP07, AP08
8Treat every model output as untrusted input. No model text straight into a shell, SQL, HTML or a fetched URL.Commands use argument lists and queries use parameters. Rendered output can't load remote images.R03
9Be able to stop it, and know you can. One person can cut off the agent (and its sub-agents) without its cooperation, and without locking out the user.You ran the stop once, timed it, and wrote down the time.R11, B04
10Log every action, not just the answer. Record tool calls, arguments, approvals, denials and results, with which agent and version did them.You can rebuild yesterday's run from the log, including what failed.R13
Add the scan to CINext

Add the scan to CI

# .github/workflows/agent-security.yml
name: Agent security
on: [pull_request]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  open-agent-security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: brace-ai-security/open-agent-security@v3.3.0   # or pin a commit SHA
        with:
          fail-on: high

Set upload-sarif: "true" and grant security-events: write to see findings as annotations on the pull request.

Badge

Once the scan passes in CI, you can show it:

[![Agent security: open-agent-security scan passing](https://img.shields.io/badge/open--agent--security-scan_passing-2ea44f)](https://braceframework.org/anti-patterns/)

The badge says only that the automated scan for known-dangerous agent setups passes. It doesn't claim that the agent completed BRACE Starter or the full checklist, so don't present it as a certification.

Next

When the agent handles money, personal data or production systems, or acts without a person watching, move to the full checklist. Use the role map to see who owns each item.
